a: More independent minters running full nodes around the world make the network more resilient and harder to censor. a: No. On Qortal the minter who signs a block earns nothing extra. Rewards are shared among all online minters by level tier, so minters don't compete with each other. Signing just moves the chain forward.

q: Who can sign new blocks on Qortal?
a: Only minters at level 5 or higher sign blocks; level 5 is when nodes start submitting blocks by default. Higher levels are more likely to be the signer, which makes attacks that need many blocks in a row very unlikely. Signing earns no extra reward.

q: What is MemPoW?
a: MemPoW is Qortal's memory-based proof of work. Each minting signature must carry a MemPoW result, computed at a fixed difficulty with about 1 MB of RAM, so it doesn't max out the CPU. Its job is to limit how many minting keys one computer can run, ideally two. Q-Chat also uses it against spam.

q: Why can a node only have two minting keys?
a: Because of MemPoW: every minting signature needs a memory-based proof of work, and one computer can only compute about two in each minting window. That stops one machine from running many minting accounts. Qortal Hub follows the same limit and won't start minting on a node that already has two minting keys.
